name: Astrocyte
short_description: Star-shaped glial support cell with many radiating processes ending in perivascular end-feet on brain capillaries; feeds and buffers neurons, recycles glutamate, and helps form the blood-brain barrier.

textbook.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; single specimen, muted desaturated educational palette matching the house style, true stellate silhouette with 8+ radiating branching processes (not a single axon), quarter cutaway soma with a small pale euchromatic nucleus (no dominant nucleolus, correctly smaller/paler than a neuron's), scattered mitochondria, a green Golgi ribbon, a pale rough-ER fold, and fine dark stippled glycogen granules; two process tips flare into flattened perivascular end-feet, one draping a short pink capillary segment at the frame edge as context only; a small dark band on one distal process tip reads as a plausible gap-junction contact point; no myelin, no axon, no text, no border, used as final on first attempt

sem.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; single specimen, false-colour warm golden-tan surface-only rendering, correct true stellate branching with repeated fine terminal twigs, two branch tips terminate into pale cream capillary segments entering from opposite corners as context, cool studio lighting, no internal organelles as expected for SEM, no baked text; used as final on first attempt)

3d.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; natural warm amber/cream biological tones, clearly distinguishable structures - pale translucent nucleus, folded rough ER, tan Golgi stack, warm-toned mitochondria with cristae, small dark glycogen dots - true stellate silhouette with many radiating branching processes, two process tips flatten into maroon perivascular end-feet, one wrapping a red-toned capillary segment at the frame edge (blood-vessel-appropriate colour), the other serving as a plausible gap-junction contact point; not near-monochrome, not neon, no text; used as final on first attempt)

watercolor.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; full-bleed warm aged paper reaching all four edges with a soft wash halo behind the subject, matching the sepia-toned naturalist-plate house look already established for this set (cf. schwann-cell watercolor final); single specimen, true stellate silhouette, fine ink linework, soma interior shows painted mitochondria ovals, a small Golgi crescent, and stippled glycogen dots; two process tips end in simple perivascular end-feet, one draped over a small red-toned capillary segment at the page margin, the other ending at a tiny painted sliver with a dark dot marking a gap-junction contact; no frame/mat/sheet-on-surface, no text; used as final on first attempt)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons "Astrocyte5.jpg", CC BY-SA 3.0, GerryShaw; real GFAP (yellow) + DAPI (blue nuclei) double immunofluorescence micrograph of a cultured human astrocyte - single dominant, clearly isolated specimen showing the diagnostic stellate morphology with dozens of fine radiating GFAP-positive processes converging on a central soma with its nucleus, surrounded by smaller unstained/counterstained cells typical of a mixed culture background; no baked-in text or scale bar to remove, single-specimen framing already clean, used as downloaded for display; see render.md §2 - two earlier candidate downloads (a dense GFAP-IHC tissue section with overlay pointer arrows, and AI-edited variants that hallucinated additional astrocyte-like cells not present in the source photo) were rejected and removed in favour of this cleaner single-specimen photograph)
